clue.text: The sort of society we're becoming? Broke!

definitions.text: The sort of society we're becoming
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a society where cards and electronic payments replace notes and coins
second meaning: having no money at all

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes it read as social commentary followed by an exclamation; the two parts are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A society without notes and coins is described this way, and so is a person who has run out of money.

clue.text: It's Cantona's thing, being one who hits out, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word for a hitter is only to be matched by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a socker is one who socks, that is punches

explanation.surface: A jibe at footballer Eric Cantona, famous for kung-fu kicking a fan in 1995.
explanation.walkthrough: Cantona was the Manchester United forward who attacked a spectator, so 'one who hits out' fits him too; the sport's name sounds like SOCKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantona was a professional footballer, so his game, his line of work, is association football.

clue.text: Superstar hideaway — taxmen get sod all

parts.note: a den is a private retreat
IR stands for the Inland Revenue, the former British tax authority
British slang for nothing, and nothing is the letter O

explanation.surface: A film star tucked away in a retreat while the tax inspectors come away empty-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: IR is the Inland Revenue, Britain's tax collector of the time; 'sod all' is crude British slang for nothing, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert De Niro is one of Hollywood's best-known film actors, an example of a screen superstar.

clue.text: Fanny wouldn't quite be seen wearing one

definitions.text: Fanny wouldn't quite be seen wearing one

parts.words: Fanny wouldn't quite be seen wearing one
parts.note: the skimpy garment covers a woman's private parts, so they are almost but not quite visible

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'fanny' means a woman's genitals, not the buttocks as in America; the name Fanny is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny thong of underwear leaves almost everything on show, so its wearer is just about covered.

clue.text: One world-rocking negotiator? Hardly

indicators.note: rocking shakes the letters of the two words about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sneer at a peace envoy who is meant to shake up the world but achieves little.
explanation.walkthrough: David Owen, made a peer, was the EU's peace negotiator in the Bosnian war; 'Hardly' mocks his lack of success.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Foreign Secretary served as co-chairman of the Yugoslavia peace conference in the early 1990s, a mediator whose plans failed.

clue.text: An outmoded burden, Di should get on back to indiscriminate USA, right?

parts.note: Princess Diana's name, taken as it is

indicators.note: back means the little word on is read the other way round
indiscriminate means without order, so the three letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Advice to Princess Diana to head off to America and escape the royal burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on back' gives NO; 'indiscriminate' jumbles USA into SAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old-fashioned and unwieldy that has outlived its time is called a prehistoric reptile, figuratively.

clue.text: In craft, Di's an expert

indicators.note: In tells us the princess's name is to be placed inside the boat

parts.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed boat, a small craft
Princess Diana's name, taken as it is

explanation.surface: Princess Diana claimed to be skilled at something crafty or practical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like skill, but it is a boat: a punt, the pole-driven boat of Oxford and Cambridge rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A commentator brought on to give an authoritative opinion is an authority or specialist in the field.

clue.text: Major back-stabber emerges from drunken bash on a stretcher

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering about, so these sixteen letters are reeled into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk is carried off on a stretcher after a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher, now in the Lords, attacked her successor John Major's policies, so 'Major' is the Prime Minister, not 'major'.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Prime Minister undermined her successor John Major publicly, making her his principal critic from behind.

clue.text: Obnoxious party-backed records of borrowing

indicators.note: backed means the word for a party is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: a do is a party
IOUs are written promises recording a debt

explanation.surface: A sneer at loans propped up by a political party's debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political, but here it is a social gathering, and the IOUs are its borrowing records.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hateful and highly offensive is objectionable in the same way as something obnoxious.

clue.text: Trendy 'Hello' from 1960s reluctant shagger

definitions.meaning: first meaning: showy and pretentious, like Hello! magazine's world
second meaning: the London Zoo giant panda who refused to mate with the Moscow panda An An

explanation.walkthrough: Hello! is a glossy British celebrity magazine; Chi Chi was London Zoo's giant panda, whose arranged matings with An An in the 1960s failed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes affectedly fashionable, frilly elegance, and was also the name of a famous zoo animal.

clue.text: A challenging bastard of very high standing in California

definitions.meaning: first meaning: John ..., one of the Tory rebels Major called bastards, who challenged him for the leadership in 1995

definitions.text: of very high standing in California
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the giant tree of the Californian coast

explanation.walkthrough: John Major was overheard calling Eurosceptic cabinet members 'bastards'; one of them stood against him for the party leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: A Conservative politician shares the name of the coast sequoia, the world's tallest tree species.

clue.text: Sort of communication that would inform Major he's been dumped?

definitions.text: Sort of communication that would inform Major he's been dumped?

parts.words: Sort of communication that would inform Major he's been dumped
parts.note: the standard break-up letter is addressed to a man by his first name, and Major's first name is John

explanation.walkthrough: The name for a letter ending a relationship happens to fit the Prime Minister John Major, as if the voters were ending things.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the familiar term for a letter in which a woman tells her partner the relationship is over.

clue.text: Means the law is corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or twisted, so the six letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A cynical observation that the legal system is crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' looks like a verb, as in 'signifies', but it is the noun meaning money.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's means are their money and resources, which taken together amount to riches.

clue.text: Screw you've really had to work for?

definitions.text: Screw you've really had to work for?

parts.words: Screw you've really had to work for
parts.note: screw is slang for wages, which are earned by working

explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' reads as sex, but it is old British slang for pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular fixed pay from an employer is a wage that has been earned through labour.

clue.text: English lass needs to get screwed outside — assistance requested by suitor

indicators.note: outside tells us the word for screwed is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: laid is slang for having had sex
gal is an informal word for a girl or lass

explanation.surface: A lewd picture of a girl and an eager suitor wanting help.
explanation.walkthrough: A suitor here is one who brings a lawsuit, not a wooer; publicly funded help with legal costs is what they ask for.
explanation.definitionFit: Public funding that pays a litigant's lawyers is help sought by someone bringing a case to court.

clue.text: Broadcast watchdog with right to eye up a lot of pussy

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to eye is to see

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: moggy is British slang for a cat

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of a regulator ogling sexual material.
explanation.walkthrough: William Rees-Mogg chaired the Broadcasting Standards Council; 'eye up' gives SEE read upwards, EES, and a moggy is a cat, with its last letter dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Times editor chaired the body set up to police sex and violence on British television.

clue.text: One took out 'one's offspring'?

parts.note: the Queen speaks of herself as one, so one's offspring is one of her children, here her second son

explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's habit of saying 'one' for 'I' is the joke; the Duke of York is her son.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Andrew is a son of Queen Elizabeth II, a child of the monarch who calls herself 'one'.

clue.text: Just the place for wet dreams?

definitions.text: Just the place for wet dreams?

parts.words: Just the place for wet dreams
parts.note: a bed filled with liquid is literally wet, and beds are where people dream

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet dreams' is a sexual phrase; read literally it describes dreaming on a mattress full of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress filled with liquid is a place to sleep, and therefore to dream, that is literally wet.

clue.text: A percentage of Brenda's lot?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a payment to an author or patent holder taken as a share of sales
second meaning: the Queen's family, as Private Eye calls the Queen 'Brenda'

explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye nicknames the Queen 'Brenda', so her lot are the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a share of earnings paid to a creator and the royal family collectively.

clue.text: There's little good in remoulding image of this woman!

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for good goes inside the rearranged letters
remoulding means shaping again, so the five letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: a little good is its abbreviation, G

explanation.surface: A sneer that no image makeover can improve a certain woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remoulding' turns IMAGE into MAGIE, and G goes inside it; the woman is Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Maggie was the popular nickname of Margaret Thatcher, the woman whose image the clue dismisses.

clue.text: Square on tv, that's Prince (formerly)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the fictional London square where the soap EastEnders is set
second meaning: Queen Victoria's husband, a prince of the nineteenth century

explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap opera set around a fictional east London square.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the soap's fictional square and to Victoria's consort, the Prince Consort.

clue.text: So presumably the stink has died down from the so-called sporting body?

definitions.text: So presumably the stink has died down from the so-called sporting body?

parts.words: So presumably the stink has died down from the so-called sporting body
parts.note: a stale smell from aged wind, and the insult England captain Will Carling used for the Rugby Football Union committee

explanation.walkthrough: In 1995 England rugby captain Will Carling called the RFU committee '57 old farts' and was briefly sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British insult for stuffy elderly men, here the rugby union's governing committee.

clue.text: Old party official's summer residence by university — a place of concentrated horror

parts.note: a dacha is a Russian country house, typical of Soviet Communist Party officials

explanation.surface: A Soviet official's holiday home beside a university, then a sudden turn to atrocity.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Nazi concentration camp, near Munich, is a site of the Holocaust's horrors.

clue.text: Community split by new gay-bashing outside bureau

indicators.note: outside tells us the jumbled letters go around the other piece
bashing means battering, so the three letters are knocked into a new order
split by means the letters for community are parted by another letter going into them

parts.note: EC is the European Community

explanation.surface: A community torn apart by new attacks on gay people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Community' is the European Community of the time, abbreviated as the two letters still used in crosswords for it.
explanation.definitionFit: An office providing a service, such as a news or travel organisation, is a bureau.

clue.text: Stuffing then gagging Di's complaint

parts.note: the eating disorder of bingeing then vomiting, which Princess Diana said she suffered

explanation.walkthrough: Princess Diana spoke publicly of her eating disorder in her 1995 Panorama interview.
explanation.definitionFit: The disorder involves binge eating followed by self-induced vomiting, as Diana described.

clue.text: Conservative leader sheer crap on tv

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of the word in front of it
crap means rubbish or badly made, so the five letters are in a mess

explanation.surface: A sneer at the Tory leader's pitiful performance on television.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the American sitcom set in a Boston bar, a hit on British TV.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitcom about a Boston bar is a programme shown on television.

clue.text: Doing what BMARC did to Iran, cultivating? F-off!

definitions.text: Doing what BMARC did to Iran

indicators.note: off means the letter F is removed from the start of the word

parts.note: farming is cultivating the land

explanation.surface: A rude dismissal of an arms firm accused of illegally supplying Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: BMARC was a British arms firm accused in the 1990s of supplying weapons to Iran; 'F-off' looks like a swear word but means drop the F.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplying a country with weapons is equipping it militarily, as the firm was alleged to have done.

clue.text: See 8
